dedupe_keys.name: rim2d gpu accelerated urban pluvial inundation model with sewer capacity drainage

description: RIM2D is a parsimonious, GPU-accelerated hydraulic model for urban pluvial flood simulation, described in a 2024 Frontiers in Water article. It treats built-up areas as flow obstacles and represents urban drainage with capacity-based approaches, infiltration on pervious surfaces and sewer drainage from roofs and sealed surfaces, not a full sewer network model. The authors validate it on eight heavy rainfall events in a Dresden test area with detailed sewer discharge measurements, and find it reproduces the temporal dynamics and volumes of sewer discharge within acceptable ranges; deviations look caused by the rainfall input, not model simplification. They conclude it is a valid urban inundation tool and that short runtimes allow probabilistic risk assessment and forecasting. Coverage: any urban area with terrain data, validated in one German test area. Access: open-access article; model distribution and the model licence were not stated on the page read; the article is CC BY. Caveats: sewer drainage is capacity-based, so surcharge and backwater effects are not simulated. It supports rapid pluvial flood hazard and forecasting studies, and relates to EPA SWMM in the catalogue as a full sewer-network alternative.
